thread.title: Smart Speakers To Emerge As 'Trojan Horse' At CES 2018 Forum | Stock News & Stock Market Analysis - IBD

author: Investor'S Business Daily
title: Smart Speakers To Emerge As 'Trojan Horse' At CES 2018 Forum | Stock News & Stock Market Analysis - IBD
text:
Reprints 
Smart speakers were hot sellers over the holiday season, especially Amazon.com 's ( AMZN ) Echo devices, but they could be just the start of a much bigger trend toward connected homes. 
And they're likely to be a major topic of conversation at the annual CES consumer electronics show in Las Vegas next week. Amazon Echo speakers with Alexa voice controls have made people comfortable with the notion of using their voice to turn on music or get weather reports and sports scores by speaking a question out loud. 
Now early adopters are wanting to control everything from door locks and garage door openers to thermostats and lighting with voice commands or by using their smartphone. 
"It really is the Trojan horse into the smart home," Marjorie Costello, editor and publisher of Consumer Electronics Online News, told Investor's Business Daily. 
Amazon's Echo Dot, which costs $49.99, has proved to be a "gateway drug" for people to get hooked on connected home technologies, she said. 
CES 2018 is likely to see many TVs, stereos and other devices that have voice controls and can be operated using smart home networks, Costello said. 
Numerous companies will be at CES showing off Wi-Fi connected devices that can link to home control networks backed by Amazon, Alphabet 's ( GOOGL ) Google, Apple ( AAPL ) and others. 
Amazon was widely seen as a winner at CES 2017 by the way it worked to get Alexa controls into everything from refrigerators to robot vacuum cleaners. Amazon is looking to continue its dominance of CES at the 2018 show by sponsoring nine conference sessions with titles such as "Amazon's Quest for Alexa to be Everywhere" and "Building a Smarter Home with Alexa." Other sessions are focused on helping companies to incorporate Alexa technology into their products. 
CES officially kicks off on Tuesday in Las Vegas after two days of preshow activity. The four-day conference is expected to attract roughly 4,000 exhibitors and more than 170,000 attendees, including more than 7,000 members of the news media. The trade show will cover more than 2.5 million net square feet of exhibit space. 
In addition to connected home technologies, other devices expected to make waves at the 2018 show include self-driving cars, augmented reality glasses, 8K super-high-definition televisions, digital health gadgets and home robots. 
The event will feature keynote presentations from Intel ( INTC ) and Ford Motor ( F ), as well as big media briefings by Nvidia ( NVDA ), Qualcomm ( QCOM ), Sony ( SNE ), Samsung and other companies.

CES 2018 could provide positive news for several publicly traded companies, including Control4 ( CTRL ) and Universal Display ( OLED ), Cowen analyst Robert Stone said in a note to clients Friday. 
Control4 is a leader in smart home technology and will be attending the show. Control4 recently acquired Ihiji, a provider of smart home remote monitoring technology, which should help the company extend its reach, he said. 
Universal Display is a key provider of materials and technology for organic light-emitting diodes used in next-generation displays and lighting. The latest big-screen OLED TVs from LG and others at CES should help Universal Display maintain its momentum, he said. 
Stone reiterated his outperform ratings on Control4 and Universal Display. He raised his price target on Control4 to 35 from 32 and kept his target on Universal Display of 195. 
Control4 shares were up 3%, near 31, in afternoon trading on the stock market today . Universal Display was up 1.8%, near 179.60. 
Also Friday, Susquehanna Financial Group analyst Mehdi Hosseini reiterated his positive rating on Universal Display and raised his price target on the stock to 215 from 195.
